text: Paulus apostolus, non ab hominibus, neque per hominem, sed per Jesum Christum et Deum Patrem, qui eum excitavit ex mortuis,
note: *Patrem* capital, God the Father (decision 20; Θεοῦ πατρός, NRSV \"God the Father\"), as Rom 1:7 and 1 Cor 1:3 *Deō Patre* (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Gratiam et pacem a Deo Patre, et Domino nostro Jesu Christo,
note: *Grātiam* keeps its capital: the greeting is its own clause after the address of 1:1–2, as your 1 Cor 1:3 and 2 Cor 1:2 (*Grātiam et pācem ā Deō Patre nostrō*, the latter after 2 Cor 1:1's comma); *Patre* capital, God the Father (decision 20), as there (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: qui se ipsum pro nostris peccatis dedidit, ut nos eriperet ex instante saeculo malo, de voluntate Dei, Patrisque nostri,
note: *Patrisque* capital, God the Father (τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἡμῶν, NRSV \"our God and Father\"; decision 20), *nostrī* lower case; *quī* lower case, the sentence running on from 1:3 (written here, as a capital changed in a layout line stops the pipeline's own lowering) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Audivistis enim, quomodo aliquando versatus sim in Judaismo: quam immodice divinam infestarem ac depopularer ecclesiam,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 1:12 ends a sentence and *Audīstis enim* opens the proof from Paul's own history (1:13–2:14), his life in Judaism (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: suum Filium in me patefacere visum est, ut eum per gentes publicarem, non equidem cum carne et sanguine contuli,
note: *Fīlium* capital, the Son of God (τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ, NRSV \"his Son\"; decision 20), as your Rom 8:3 *Deus Fīlium suum*; *suum* lower case, the sentence of 1:15 running on after its parenthesis (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Deinde post annos tres Hierosolymam adscendi, visendi Petri gratia, apud quem etiam mansi dies quindecim.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 1:17 ends a sentence and *Deinde post annōs trēs* opens a new step of the narrative, the first visit to Jerusalem (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Eram autem ignotus facie christianis Judaeae ecclesiis.
note: *chrīstiānīs* lower case: an adjective with *ecclēsiīs* (\"the Christian churches of Judaea\", ταῖς ἐν Χριστῷ), as your 2 Cor 12:2 *hominem chrīstiānum* and Rom 15:29 *chrīstiānī ēvangeliī*; the noun stays capital (1 Cor 15:23, 2 Cor 11:3 *Chrīstiānīs*) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Ego vero, qui viderem, eos non recto pede incedere ad evangelii veritatem, dixi Petro coram omnibus: “Si tu Judaeus alienigenarum more vivis, non Judaeorum, cur alienigenas judaizare cogis?”
note: Paul's words to Peter after *dīxī Petrō cōram omnibus:* are direct (*tū … vīvis … cōgis*): in “…”, *Sī* capital as 1573 (*Si tu Iudæus*, canvas 889); closed at the end of the verse, as the BSB (the NRSV runs the speech on to 2:21; Castellio's *Nōs nātūrā Jūdæī* in 2:15 could be either); *cōgis?* with 1573's question mark (*cur alienigenas Iudaizare cogis ?*; τί … ἀναγκάζεις;) for the draft's full stop (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Nos natura Judaei, non ex alienigenis sontes,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): the words to Peter close with 2:14's question, and *Nōs nātūrā Jūdæī* opens Paul's statement of justification by faith (2:15–21) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Crucifixus sum cum Christo. Vivo autem, non jam ego, sed vivit in me Christus. Quod vero nunc in carne vivo, fide vivo Filii Dei, qui me adeo amavit, ut se ipsum pro me dederet.
note: *Fīliī Deī* capital, the Son of God (τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ; decision 20), as your Rom 1:4 *Deī Fīliō* and 2 Cor 1:19 *Deī Fīlius* (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Hoc tantum volo a vobis discere, per legis opera Spiritum acceperitis, an per orationem fidei?
note: *Spīritum* capital, the Holy Spirit the Galatians received (τὸ πνεῦμα ἐλάβετε, NRSV \"Did you receive the Spirit\"; decision 20) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Adeone dementes estis, ut a Spiritu exorsi, nunc in carnem desinatis?
note: *Spīritū* capital, as the NRSV (\"Having started with the Spirit\") and the BSB, the Spirit of 3:2 (decision 20); *carnem* lower case (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Utrumne qui vobis Spiritum suggessit, et apud vos portentosa fecit, id per legis opera fecit, an per orationem fidei?
note: *Spīritum* capital, as 3:2 (NRSV \"supplies you with the Spirit\"; decision 20) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quemadmodum \\qt “Abrahamus Deo credidit, id quod ei justitiae ductum est.”\\qt*
note: Gen 15:6 in \\qt with “…”, prose, as the BSB quotes it: the words are Castellio's own rendering of the verse as your Rom 4:3 settles it in \\qt (*Crēdidit autem Abrāhāmus Deō, id quod eī jūstitiæ ductum est*), here without a formula, *Quemadmodum* (καθώς) outside the marks as your Rom 9:7 *Sed* and 10:18 *cum*; the least certain of the quotations (it can be read as Paul's own comparison) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Neminem autem lege fieri justum apud Deum, hinc perspicuum est, quod \\qt “justus per fidem vivet.”\\qt*
note: Hab 2:4 (the BSB quotes it), the words your Rom 1:17 settles in \\qt (*Jūstus autem fidē vīvet*): in \\qt with “…” after *quod* (ὅτι), in lower case inside Paul's sentence as your Rom 10:18 *cum \\qt “in omnēs terrās …”\\qt** and Rom 9:7; the verb stays the prophet's future indicative, so quoted, not reported (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Atqui lex non est ex fide, sed \\qt “qui homo illa fecerit, per ea vivet.”\\qt*
note: Lev 18:5 (the BSB quotes it), in \\qt with “…” after *sed* (ἀλλ᾿), lower case inside the sentence as your Rom 9:7 *Sed \\qt “ab Isaacō …”\\qt**; direct words (finite *fēcerit … vīvet*), unlike your Rom 10:5, where Castellio reports the same verse (*hominem … vīctūrum esse*) and it stands unmarked (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Abrahamo autem promissa sunt illa, et ejus semini. Non dicit: “et seminibus,” quasi de multis, sed ut de uno: \\qt “et semini tuo,”\\qt* qui Christus est.
note: *et sēminī tuō* (Gen 22:18, καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου) is Scripture quoted after *Nōn dīcit … sed ut dē ūnō:*, in \\qt with “…”; *et sēminibus* is the reading Scripture does not have, words named, so in “…” without \\qt (decision 39, as 2 Cor 1:17–20), both as the BSB (\"and to seeds\", \"and to your seed\"); lower case *et* as the draft (a fragment inside the sentence); the commas inside the marks, as your 2 Cor 1:18 *“etiam,”* and 6:17 *separāminī,”* (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quorsum ergo lex? delictorum caussa adjecta est, donec veniret semen, cui promissum erat: instituta per angelos, lata per sequestrum.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 3:18 ends a sentence and *Quōrsum ergō lēx?* opens a new question, the purpose of the law (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Ergone lex est contraria Dei promissis? nequaquam. Si enim data lex esset, quae vitam conferre posset, plane in lege sita foret justitia.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 3:20 ends a sentence and *Ergōne lēx est contrāria …?* opens the next question, as 3:19 (and the NRSV's break) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Sed postquam plenum tempus advenit, misit Deus Filium suum, ex muliere natum, qui sub lege fuit,
note: *Fīlium* capital, the Son of God (τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ; decision 20), as 1:16; *fuit,* with a comma, as 1573 (*qui ſub lege fuit, … 5 vt legi ſubditos*, canvas 891), for the draft's full stop: 4:5's purpose clause (ἵνα) continues the sentence, so it starts in lower case (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Et quoniam filii estis, misit Deus Filii sui Spiritum in vestros animos, qui clamet: “Abba, Pater.”
note: the cry after *quī clāmet:* in “…” as your Rom 8:15 (*per quem clāmāmus, “Abba, Pater.”*), with its comma and *Pater* capital (God the Father; Ἀββᾶ ὁ πατήρ, decision 20); *Fīliī* capital, the Son (decision 20), *fīliī estis* lower (the believers); *estis,* with a comma, as 1573 (*Et quoniam filij eſtis, mifit Deus*, canvas 891) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Filioli mei, quos iterum parturio, donec formetur in vobis Christus:
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 4:18 ends a sentence and Paul turns to direct, tender address (*Fīliolī meī*), the appeal of 4:19–20 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Scriptum est enim: \\q1 \\qt “Laetare sterilis,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt quae non paris:\\qt* \\q1 \\qt erumpe in clamorem,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt quae non eniteris.\\qt* \\q1 \\qt Nam plures futuri sunt desertae nati,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt quam virum habentis.”\\qt*
note: Isa 54:1 after *Scrīptum est enim:* as poetry in \\qt, six lines after the BSB (the Latin's order matches its lines), mid-verse as your 2 Cor 8:15; *Lætāre* capital, the quotation's first word (the draft *laetare*); *Nam* keeps its capital after the full stop (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Nos vero, fratres, quemadmodum Isaacus, promissionis nati sumus.
note: prose again after the poetry of 4:27, as a new paragraph (the BSB's b m): *Nōs vērō, frātrēs* applies the allegory to the readers, in direct address (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Verum quid ajunt litterae? \\qt “Ejice ancillam, ejusque filium: non enim heres erit ancillae filius cum liberae filio.”\\qt*
note: Gen 21:10 after *Vērum quid ajunt litteræ?* in \\qt with “…”, prose as the BSB, as your Rom 10:8 (*Sed quid ajunt litteræ? \\qt “Ōrātiō …”\\qt**) and Rom 11:4 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: En ego Paulus vobis dico, si circumcidemini, Christus nihil vobis proderit.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 5:1 closes the allegory with its exhortation, and *Ēn ego Paulus vōbīs dīcō* opens a solemn new step, the warning against circumcision (5:2–6) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Vos enim ad libertatem vocati estis, fratres, modo ne libertate ad libidinem abutamini, sed per caritatem alius alii serviatis.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break; the NRSV's too): 5:12 ends a sentence and *Vōs enim ad lībertātem vocātī estis, frātrēs* opens the exhortation on the use of freedom, in direct address (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Nam tota lex in uno dicto comprehenditur, videlicet: \\qt “Alterum ut teipsum diligito.”\\qt*
note: Lev 19:18 after *vidēlicet:* in \\qt with “…”, prose as the BSB, as your Rom 13:9 (*in hōc dictō summātim comprehenditur: \\qt “Alterum ut teipsum amātō.”\\qt**); *Alterum* capital, as 1573 (*videlicet, Alterum vt teipſum diligito*, canvas 892) and Rom 13:9 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Sunt autem manifesta carnis opera, videlicet adulterium, stuprum, impuritas, salacitas,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 5:18 ends a sentence and *Sunt autem manifesta carnis opera* opens the list of the works of the flesh (5:19–21), set against the fruit of the Spirit (5:22–23, left in the same paragraph) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Domini nostri Jesu Christi gratia adsit animis vestris, fratres. Amen. \\cls Ad Galatas scripta est Romae.
note: the subscription set apart as \\cls after the verse (decision 37), as 1573 sets it in italics under the blessing (canvas 892) and as your Rom 16:27, 1 Cor 16:24 and 2 Cor 13:14; *frātrēs.* with a full stop before *Āmēn*, as 1573 (*veſtris, fratres. Amen.*) and 2 Cor 13:14, for the draft's colon (Claude, 2026-11-11)
